historical_anchor: Historically Takagi ordered 18 available Sixth Fleet submarines toward positions east of the Marianas after A-GO activation.

Historically the Saipan invasion disrupted Sixth Fleet communications and control shifted to Owada at Truk; subsequent radio orders and fixed patrol-line geometry were vulnerable to US intelligence and ASW.
I-10 had already reconnoitered an empty Majuro anchorage on 12 Jun, an important Japanese cue that the US fast carriers were at sea.

branch_command_change.predelegation: Because Japanese ISR had rated Marianas CRITICAL before D-Day, Combined Fleet requires a pre-planned alternate submarine-control handoff to Truk rather than improvising it after Saipan communications fail.
branch_command_change.handoff: As Saipan headquarters circuits degrade during 15 Jun, operational control passes to Owada/Truk on a prearranged schedule with acknowledgement windows. Takagi remains physically on Saipan but loss of his headquarters does not erase submarine tasking.
branch_command_change.COMSEC_effect: No broad message containing the full exact patrol-line coordinate set is transmitted in a form the branch treats as routinely decryptable high-grade traffic. Boats receive sector boxes, time gates and sparse update groups. US DF and traffic analysis still infer activity but not a ready-made kill map.

working_force_state.branch_operational_interpretation: Use roughly historical high-teens immediately available/converging strength as the hard center; branch extra submarine survivals are not automatically added until named-hull routing is closed.
sector_scheme: outer eastward transport/support and recontact sectors
working_force_state.not_yet_on_station: Several long-range I/RO boats are still converging and cannot be credited as if already sitting on the US carrier track.

15Jun_contacts.amphibious_force: At least one RO/I-boat obtains hydrophone/periscope-quality confirmation of dense amphibious/support traffic and the eastward night movement of vulnerable transports. This is useful operational confirmation but not a surprise discovery.
15Jun_contacts.fast_carrier_force: One outer-sector report produces a PROBABLE fast-carrier/support sector east of the Marianas, with roughly 80-140 nmi uncertainty and several-hour staleness. It is not good enough for a same-day mobile-fleet strike.
15Jun_contacts.attack_result: No confirmed Japanese submarine torpedo hit on a US capital ship/transport on 15 Jun. Heavy destroyer, CVE air-ASW and patrol-air density keep approach quality low.

future_effect: The branch enters 16-19 Jun with a more coherent Japanese submarine scouting net and without the historical automatic high-grade-code compromise of exact fixed patrol positions. US radar/air-ASW remains dangerous, so this is an ISR improvement, not submarine immunity.
